desc:
Ecommerce keyword research and mapping finds the words your shoppers really type and assigns each one to the right page of your store. Ecom Swift LLC delivers a clean spreadsheet that shows what to write, rename or build next.

## What is ecommerce keyword research and mapping?

Ecommerce keyword research is the process of finding the phrases shoppers use when they look for products like yours, and keyword mapping is the step of giving each phrase a home on your site. The result is a sheet where every important term points to one page: a product, a collection or a guide.

The mapping matters as much as the list. A long list of keywords with no plan is just a spreadsheet of ideas. A map tells you which page should target which phrase, so two pages never fight for the same search.

## Why guessing your keywords costs you visitors

Owners often name products the way their supplier does, or the way they speak among themselves. Shoppers use different words. A store may call an item a "lounge set" while customers search for "matching pajama set", and the store never appears for the phrase people use.

Wrong wording is quiet loss. Nothing breaks and no error shows. The right visitors simply never arrive, because your pages do not match what they typed.

## How keyword choices affect traffic and sales

Each search phrase signals a different stage of buying. Short, broad phrases show curiosity. Longer, specific phrases, such as a product type with a size, material or use, usually come from people close to buying. Research separates the two so you can aim your product pages at ready buyers and your guides at those still comparing.

Checking how crowded the results are matters too. A phrase with strong demand but dominated by large retailers may be the wrong target for a small store, while a narrower phrase can bring steadier, more relevant visits. We describe demand and competition as notes to guide your choices, not as promises about where a page will land.

## What a useful keyword map contains

- Each keyword with a short note on demand and competition.
- Phrases grouped by topic, so related terms sit together.
- The recommended page for every keyword, existing or new.
- Buying intent marked clearly on each term.
- Suggested page titles built around the main phrase.
- Gaps where competitors appear and your store does not.
- Terms that tie to seasons, with notes on timing.
- Ideas for guides and pages that do not yet exist.
- Words to avoid because they attract the wrong visitor.

## How we do the research

We start with your products and your customers: what you sell, how people describe it and who competes with you. We then gather candidate phrases from search data, competitor pages and the questions shoppers ask, and check each one for demand and difficulty.

Next we group the terms by topic and match each to a page. Where no suitable page exists, we mark it as a new page or guide. Everything arrives in one spreadsheet that you can read without special tools.

The Basic package covers a starter set of products or collections with each keyword matched to a page. The Standard package widens the map, marks buying intent, reviews competitor gaps and suggests titles. The Premium package covers a large catalog, adds ideas for new pages and guides, notes seasonal terms and includes a walkthrough call. Add-ons cover extra pages, a local keyword set and question phrases.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Use one main phrase per page, with a few close variants.
- Write product names the way customers say them.
- Update the map when you add new product lines.
- Choose phrases you can honestly satisfy with your pages.
- Use the map before you write new text, not after.

**Avoid:**
- Targeting the same phrase on several pages.
- Chasing only the biggest, most crowded terms.
- Repeating a keyword unnaturally in every sentence.
- Ignoring long phrases that show clear buying intent.
- Treating the list as finished forever, since search habits change.

## Who this service is for

A new seller who has not yet written product pages can use the map to name and structure the store properly. An existing store with weak traffic may find its pages simply use different words from its customers. A shop planning a content or blog programme needs the research first, so articles aim at real questions.

It also suits owners about to hire a writer, since the map gives that writer a clear brief.

## What we need from you

Send your store address or product list, plus the markets and countries you sell to. If you know your main competitors, include them. We do not need your password. If we need to see your search data, you can add us as a viewer on Search Console. We do not need to edit your store for research, and the sheet is yours to keep.
